chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Three [groups of] people are the closest to God on the Day of Resurrection until the people are finished with the Reckoning: A man whose power/authority did not compel him, in his state of anger, to oppress those under his command; a man who walked among two people and did not favor one over the other in any matter; and a man who spoke the truth whether it was in his favor or against him.

key_terms.فِيمَا لَهُ وَعَلَيْهِ: In what is for him and against him

ai.seo_question: Who are the three groups of people closest to God on the Day of Resurrection according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three archetypes—just leadership, impartial mediation, and courageous truthfulness—as the pinnacle of moral conduct that secures divine proximity. This classification reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing personal piety with social justice, where integrity in power, fairness in conflict, and honesty in obligation are paramount. The hadith underscores that true closeness to God is demonstrated through consistent ethical action in worldly affairs rather than mere ritual observance.
